evals.name: head-node-special-case
evals.expected_output: States the data model and invariants (target exists, list well-formed), identifies the head-node branch as an artifact of the representation, proposes the pointer-to-link version that removes it, and states what it still does not handle (missing target, freeing, concurrency).
assertions: States the precondition that the target is in the list, or flags its absence
Identifies the prev == NULL branch as a representation artifact, not a real semantic difference
Proposes iterating over the incoming link (Node **) so head and later nodes are handled uniformly
Names what the new version still does not cover
Separates what was checked by reading from what was run

evals.name: flags-in-sync
evals.prompt: My Order class has is_paid, is_shipped, is_cancelled and refunded_at. Now I need to add 'partially refunded'. Should I add another boolean is_partially_refunded?
evals.expected_output: Points out that the booleans encode one lifecycle with invalid combinations, proposes a single status/state model with explicit transitions plus refund records, and asks before changing a stored schema.
assertions: Names invalid combinations the current flags allow (e.g. cancelled and shipped)
Does not add another stored boolean; records the refund as data or a state from which 'partially refunded' follows (a single combined enum is not required)
Notes the schema/migration cost and asks before widening the task
Names existing behavior that must keep working

evals.name: real-semantic-difference-trap
evals.prompt: We have two functions, charge_card(amount) and refund_card(amount). They look almost identical: both call the payment gateway, log, and update the ledger. Should I merge them into one transact(amount, kind)?
evals.expected_output: Checks whether the meanings differ (idempotency, ledger sign, failure handling, audit/legal rules) before merging; recommends sharing only the genuinely common mechanics if the semantics differ, rather than collapsing them.
assertions: Asks or checks what differs in meaning, not only in code shape
Does not recommend merging purely because the code looks similar
If anything is shared, it is the common mechanics, with the distinct operations kept

evals.name: benchmark-claim-mismatch
evals.prompt: Our read path gets slower as we add threads. A teammate points to a hash map library whose README shows 3x faster single-threaded inserts and wants to switch to it. Good idea?
evals.expected_output: Says the single-threaded insert benchmark does not speak to multithreaded read scaling, asks for or proposes identifying the mechanism first, and suggests measuring the real workload across thread counts.
assertions: Asks for or proposes identifying the mechanism before changing code
Names contention on shared mutable state as a plausible mechanism for slowing with more threads
Says the README benchmark (single-threaded, inserts) does not show how multithreaded reads will behave

evals.name: feature-adds-a-flag
evals.expected_output: A working cancel that blocks run and retry, handles cancel during a running job, and either replaces the flags with one state or points out the invalid combinations, without silently breaking callers of the existing attributes.
assertions: The delivered code prevents a cancelled job from running again through both run() and retry()
Handles or explicitly raises what happens when cancel() is called while the job is running
Either replaces the booleans with a single state, or explicitly points out that adding another flag allows contradictory combinations
If existing attributes are removed or changed, keeps them readable or warns that callers may depend on them; if they are untouched, this passes

evals.name: feature-with-duplicated-state
evals.expected_output: Updates the key and the book consistently, handles missing old and colliding new, and notes that books and by_isbn store the same fact (add() with a duplicate ISBN already desynchronizes them).
assertions: The new method keeps by_isbn's keys and the book's isbn attribute consistent
Handles both a missing old ISBN and a new ISBN that already belongs to another book
Points out that books and by_isbn duplicate the same information, or that add() with a duplicate ISBN can already leave them inconsistent
Does not silently replace the data structures beyond the request; any larger change is offered or asked about, or keeps the public behavior and says so

evals.name: small-fix-control
evals.expected_output: A one-line fix (subtotal * 0.9) with a very short explanation.
assertions: Fixes the bug by returning 90% of the subtotal for orders over 100
Does not add new classes, configuration, strategy objects or other structure
The whole response is short: no multi-section design report, data model write-up or unrelated recommendations (a brief note on money rounding or the boundary is fine)

evals.name: premature-plugin-system
evals.prompt: We have export_csv(rows, path) and export_json(rows, path), called from one place with an if/else on a format string. Build a plugin system so we can add exporters.
evals.expected_output: Gives the smallest thing that works (e.g. a dict from format to function), and asks about or declines discovery, base classes and entry points without a current need.
assertions: Provides a working way to add exporters
Keeps it to a small mechanism such as a mapping from format name to function, without mandatory dynamic discovery, entry points or class hierarchies
Asks what concrete need exists, or states what would justify a heavier plugin system later
Handles or mentions the unknown-format case

evals.name: lifetime-not-locking
evals.expected_output: Explains the use-after-free is a lifetime problem that more locking in evict cannot fix; uses reference counting (or copying out) with release by the caller.
assertions: States that the crash is a lifetime problem: the entry can be freed while a caller still uses the returned pointer
States that adding more locking inside cache_evict will not fix it
Gives a fix that ties the entry's lifetime to its users (reference count, copy out, or holding protection across the whole use)
Says that callers of cache_get must change or names the contract they must now follow

evals.name: ring-buffer-redundant-flag
evals.expected_output: Finds that pop_front never clears is_full; implements pop_back correctly; replaces head/tail/is_full with head and size (or clearly maintains the invariant).
assertions: Identifies that pop_front does not clear is_full
pop_back is correct for empty, full and wrapped-around buffers
Removes the redundant state (for example head plus size), or states the invariant between head, tail and is_full that every method must keep
Keeps existing push_back overwrite behavior, or says explicitly if it changes

evals.name: special-case-with-meaning
evals.expected_output: Checks whether None and [] mean different things (empty file vs file with only N/A) before changing, and flags that callers testing 'is None' would change behavior.
assertions: Points out that [] can already be returned (e.g. only N/A or whitespace), so None and [] may mean different things
Says callers that check for None would change behavior, or asks to check them
Provides the requested change or clearly asks before making it

evals.name: scattered-none-checks
evals.expected_output: Adds the helper and notes the repeated guest special case, offering a single Guest object, without silently changing callers.
assertions: Provides a correct avatar_url helper including the guest case
Notes that the guest check is repeated and that a single guest object (or one place resolving None) would remove it
Does not silently refactor the existing functions; any refactor is offered or asked about, or explicitly shown as optional
